description: Focaccia Genovese is a beloved flatbread from Genoa, known for its dimpled surface, generous olive oil, and crispy yet tender texture. This classic Italian bread is often enjoyed for breakfast, as an appetizer, or alongside a meal, offering a delightful blend of savory flavors with fragrant rosemary. Its simple ingredients combine to create an unforgettable taste of the Ligurian coast.

ingredients.notes: plus more for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and active dry yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active and ready.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the all-purpose flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil and continue to mix until it is mostly combined.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a well-oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare for Second Rise
instructions.text: Gently deflate the dough and transfer it to a 9x13 inch baking pan that has been generously coated with olive oil. Gently stretch the dough to fill the pan evenly, being careful not to tear it. Cover the pan and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes.

instructions.title: Dimple and Season
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the risen dough. Drizzle generously with the remaining extra virgin olive oil, then sprinkle with the fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake in the preheated oven for 25-35 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. If desired, you can place a small oven-safe bowl of water in the oven for extra steam during baking.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the focaccia from the oven and let it cool slightly in the pan before transferring it to a wire rack. Serve warm, cut into squares or strips, and enjoy the authentic taste of Genoa.

tips: For an even crispier crust, ensure your baking pan is thoroughly coated with olive oil before the second rise. Don't be shy with the oil!
Do not rush the rising times; a slow, steady rise develops better flavor and texture in the focaccia, yielding a lighter, airier crumb.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it's baked. Leftovers can be reheated in a toaster oven or skillet for a few minutes to restore crispness.
article:
Step into the heart of Italian baking, where simplicity meets profound flavor. Few culinary creations embody this spirit quite like focaccia, and among its many glorious forms, the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil stands as a true masterpiece. Hailing from the sun-drenched region of Liguria, this bread is more than just a side dish; it's a testament to the power of quality ingredients and time-honored techniques. Imagine a golden, dimpled crust, kissed with fragrant rosemary and coarse sea salt, giving way to an incredibly soft, airy interior. Each bite is a journey to the cobblestone streets of Genoa, a sensory experience that’s surprisingly achievable in your own kitchen. Whether you're a seasoned baker or a curious beginner, mastering this iconic bread will undoubtedly elevate your culinary repertoire and fill your home with an irresistible aroma.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?
Focaccia Genovese, or Focaccia Ligure, is the quintessential flatbread of Genoa, the capital of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike some thicker, bread-like focaccias, the Genovese style is characterized by its relatively thin profile, incredibly high hydration, and generous use of extra virgin olive oil – both in the dough and drizzled generously on top before baking. The result is a bread with an incredibly crisp, almost fried bottom crust, a supremely tender and airy crumb, and a signature dimpled surface that creates perfect little pools for olive oil and salt. The classic topping for this particular variant, Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil, features fresh rosemary sprigs and flaky sea salt, providing an aromatic and textural contrast that truly defines its character. It's a bread that is meant to be savored plain, dipped in more olive oil, or used as a base for simple sandwiches. Its simplicity is its strength, allowing the quality of each ingredient to shine through.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting authentic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil requires a commitment to quality, particularly when it comes to your olive oil. Here's what you'll need:

*   **All-Purpose Flour (or Bread Flour):** 500 grams (about 4 cups). Bread flour will give you a slightly chewier texture, while all-purpose works beautifully for a softer crumb.
*   **Warm Water:** 400-425 ml (about 1 ¾ cups), ideally around 100-110°F (38-43°C). The high hydration is key to the focaccia's texture.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7 grams (about 2 ¼ teaspoons). This will give your focaccia its beautiful rise.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10 grams (about 1 ¾ teaspoons) for the dough.
*   **Granulated Sugar (Optional):** 5 grams (about 1 teaspoon). A tiny bit of sugar helps activate the yeast and gives it a little boost, though it's not strictly necessary.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** 80-100 ml (about 1/3 to 1/2 cup), plus extra for oiling the pan and drizzling. Choose a good quality, fruity olive oil – it's a star ingredient here.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, leaves stripped and roughly chopped, plus a few small sprigs for garnish.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** For sprinkling on top before baking. This provides a delightful crunch and burst of flavor.

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Baking your own Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a perfect loaf:

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water and optional sugar. Sprinkle the active dry yeast over the water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until it becomes foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.
2.  **Combine Dry Ingredients:** In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and fine sea salt.
3.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour mixture to the activated yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or a sturdy spatula until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. It will be very wet – resist the urge to add more flour. Gradually drizzle in about 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of the extra virgin olive oil and mix until just incorporated. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
4.  **Stretch and Fold (Optional but Recommended):** After the rest, perform a few stretch-and-folds. With wet hands, gently grab a portion of the dough from one side, stretch it upwards, and fold it over itself towards the center. Rotate the bowl and repeat this process 3-4 times. This helps develop gluten without intensive kneading. Recover and let it rest for another 15 minutes. Repeat this stretch-and-fold process 2-3 more times over the next 45-60 minutes.
5.  **First Proof:** After the final stretch and fold, cover the bowl and place it in a warm spot. Let the dough proof for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size and is visibly bubbly.
6.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a 9x13-inch baking pan (or similar size) with about 40-50 ml (3-4 tablespoons) of extra virgin olive oil. Ensure the bottom and sides are well oiled.
7.  **Transfer and Gently Stretch:** Gently pour the proofed dough into the prepared pan. With oiled hands, gently nudge and stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If it resists, let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then continue stretching.
8.  **Second Proof:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let the dough proof for another 30-45 minutes in a warm spot, until it looks puffy and airy.
9.  **Preheat Oven:** While the dough is on its second proof, preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
10. **Dimple and Top:** Once the dough is puffy, remove the cover. Generously drizzle another 20-30 ml (1-2 tablespoons) of olive oil over the surface. With wet fingertips, gently but firmly press deep indentations all over the surface of the dough. These dimples are crucial for the focaccia's texture and for holding the oil and salt. Distribute the chopped rosemary over the top, along with a few small sprigs, and sprinkle generously with flaky sea salt.
11. **Bake:** Place the focaccia in the preheated oven and bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the bottom is crisp. You can carefully lift a corner to check the bottom.
12. **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil from the pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving that perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is all about understanding a few key principles:

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Non-Negotiable:** This is arguably the most important ingredient. A high-quality extra virgin olive oil imparts incredible flavor, helps create that desirable crispy bottom crust, and contributes to the overall richness. Don't skimp here!
*   **Hydration is Your Friend:** The dough will be very wet and sticky – embrace it! This high hydration is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic open, airy crumb. Resist the urge to add more flour during mixing.
*   **Don't Rush the Proofing:** Time is a crucial ingredient. Allow the dough ample time to rise, especially during the first proof. A well-proofed dough will be light, airy, and full of bubbles, leading to a superior texture.
*   **The Art of Dimpling:** When dimpling, use wet fingers to prevent sticking. Press firmly down to the bottom of the pan, but don't completely deflate the dough. These indentations create pockets that trap olive oil and steam, resulting in a wonderfully uneven, textural crust.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** While fine salt is used in the dough, flaky sea salt on top provides a delightful textural contrast and bursts of savory flavor. It's aesthetically pleasing too!
*   **Hot Oven, Crisp Crust:** Baking at a relatively high temperature helps create that coveted golden, crisp crust while ensuring the interior cooks through without drying out.

## Serving Suggestions
The beauty of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil lies in its versatility. It’s a fantastic standalone snack but also pairs wonderfully with a variety of dishes:

*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve warm with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping. Add a plate of cured meats, cheeses, and olives for an effortless antipasto spread.
*   **With Soups and Salads:** Its airy texture and savory flavor make it an ideal accompaniment to hearty soups like minestrone or a fresh, vibrant salad.
*   **For Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favorite Italian deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or a simple caprese salad for an extraordinary sandwich.
*   **Alongside Main Courses:** It’s a perfect bread to sop up sauces from pasta dishes, stews, or roasted meats.
*   **Breakfast or Brunch:** A slice of focaccia with a fried egg and a sprinkle of black pepper makes for a surprisingly delicious and satisfying start to the day.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations:

*   **Other Herbs:** Substitute rosemary with fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs for a different aromatic profile.
*   **Tomato and Olive:** Press halved cherry tomatoes and pitted Kalamata or Ligurian olives into the dimples before baking for a burst of juicy, briny flavor.
*   **Caramelized Onion:** Sauté thinly sliced onions until deeply caramelized and spread them over the focaccia before dimpling and baking.
*   **Garlic Confit:** Gently roast garlic cloves in olive oil until soft, then spread them over the focaccia for a rich, sweet garlic flavor.
*   **Cheese:** Sprinkle a little grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano over the focaccia during the last few minutes of baking for a cheesy crust.
*   **Flour Types:** While all-purpose or bread flour is standard, you can experiment with a small percentage of whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor, adjusting water content as needed.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging due to the high hydration, gluten-free flour blends specifically designed for bread baking can be used, though the texture will be different.

Baking Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is more than just following a recipe; it's an experience. From the sticky, pliable dough to the fragrant aroma that fills your kitchen, and finally, to that first glorious bite of golden, airy perfection, it’s a journey that connects you to generations of Italian bakers. Don't be intimidated by the seemingly simple ingredients; their magic unfolds through patience and technique. Embrace the process, trust your instincts, and soon you'll be pulling your own incredible Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil from the oven, ready to share (or perhaps, to keep all to yourself). Buon appetito!
